author: Mark Atwood
text:
Trait-shape API break with canonical-template propagation — needs explicit owner approval.

The bead documents three independent contract issues with is_per_user_property:
 (1) static (no &self) — locks out per-account variance.
 (2) hardcoded list in trait default — re-shipping the crate on every draft revision.
 (3) diverges from canonical sibling shape (calendars has the analog as a FREE FN in jmap-calendars-types, not a trait method).

Recommendation: option (a) move the function to jmap-tasks-types::backend as a free fn is_per_user_task_property(prop: &str) -> bool, mirroring jmap-calendars-types::is_per_user_calendar_event_property. Remove the trait method. Handler call site changes from B::is_per_user_property(head) to jmap_tasks_types::is_per_user_task_property(head).

Rationale:
 - Closes (3) by structural parity with the canonical sibling.
 - Closes (2) partially — list is still in this workspace's type crate, but moving it to types-crate is the right place for spec-canonical classification.
 - (1) — per-account variance is a real concern only for vendor-extension backends; the canonical (sibling) shape doesn't allow it either. Defer.

This is the workspace-canonical shape and the bead is exactly the kind of 'symmetry break' the canonical-template rule was written to prevent. But: it's a public-API breaking change on jmap-tasks-server (removes a trait method) plus an additive change on jmap-tasks-types (new pub fn). Pre-publish crates make the cost low; canonical-template parity makes the benefit clear.

Escalating because (a) is a coordinated multi-crate API break and the related bead JMAP-h47t.2 already shipped a fix that calls B::is_per_user_property — replacing that call site is part of this change.
